text:
mira: Heads up — we've got a subtle peering timing drift between eu-west1 <-> ap-southeast1. Seeing short RTT spikes (~200-400ms) causing apiserver leader lease renewals to miss and controller-manager reconcile queues to grow. GPU provisioner reacted and started extra allocations in ap-southeast, pushing cost + latency. ping graph: https://grafana.internal/r/peering-drift

ash: copying metrics, seeing leader election retries on apiserver pods? what do logs show for lease renewals?

henry: logs from apiserver leader: 
```
I0523 09:12:10.123 1 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out waiting for the condition
I0523 09:12:10.124 1 leaderelection.go:254] attempting to acquire leader lease...
```
controller-manager backlog +50k items in 3m.

lena: that RTT bump is right at the threshold for our leaseRenewDeadline (10s) + renew jitter. If jitter + transient RTT > renewDeadline, renew fails and leadership hops.

mira: nailed it. Controller-manager restarts or leader hops cause temporary double-scheduling signals to provisioner which thinks pods didn't bind. Result: parallel GPU reservations.

ash: quick mitigation — can we increase `--leader-elect-lease-duration` or bump `--leader-elect-renew-deadline` on controller-manager as a hotfix? Also consider rate-limit the provisioner on requeues for 2m to avoid double allocate.

henry: I can push a canary: bump renew-deadline to 20s and lease duration to 60s for controller-manager in eu-west / ap-southeast K8s clusters. Will do for one control-plane replica first.

mira: go ahead. Also open NAT egress scaling for the peering routers to reduce queueing. ops-bot, can you spin up one extra egress instance in ap-southeast? @ops-bot start-egress ap-southeast1 +1

ops-bot: Command accepted: scaling egress-gw-ap-southeast1 from 3 -> 4. ETA 45s. :gear:

samir: alternative non-invasive: add a small debounce on provisioner: if workload appears unbound, wait 30s before creating new GPU reservation when there's recent leader-change events. Would that avoid immediate double alloc?

lena: yes, a short debounce tied to leader-election events would help, but it's a code change and needs testing. Hotfix for config is faster.

ash: patch applied to controller-manager canary: `--leader-election-renew-deadline=20s --leader-election-lease-duration=60s` on eu-west1 canary replica. Observing leader held for 4m with no hops so far.

henry: provisioner requeues dropping after change. GPU reservations rate down ~70% from the spike. cost meter: https://billing.internal/graphs/gpu-overprovision-ap-southeast?from=now-6h

mira: good. Next: schedule config rollout to other clusters with small staged windows and monitor apiserver metrics. Also file a follow-up to investigate peering QoS shaping — these were very small RTT blips, maybe kernel NIC interrupt coalescing changed after latest kernel bump.

ash: reproduction steps captured:
```
# run a steady leader lease churn generator + small RTT jitter (200-400ms)
kubectl exec -n kube-system leader-tester -- ./flux --lease 10s --jitter 0.1
# observe leaderelection.go logs and controller-manager queue length
```

samir: logging note — add an explicit metric for "leader_renew_failures" emitted by apiserver leader-elections (label: region, instance) so we can alert before controller backlog grows.

mira: agreed. Create an alert: leader_renew_failures{region=~"(eu-.*|ap-.*)"} > 5 over 2m -> P2.

lena: also add a safeguard in provisioner: if controller-manager has leader changes >3 within 5m, throttle new allocations for 2m. That'll be a small defensive change.

henry: timeline: canary config changed 09:16, egress scaled 09:17, provisioner throttle applied via admission webhook tweak 09:20 canary. System steady now at 09:23.

ash: costs: one-off ~+4% GPU hourly bill during the spike window. We should include that number in postmortem.

mira: opening postmortem ticket now — assign to networking + controller teams. Action items:
- short: roll controller-manager lease config to all clusters (staged)
- short: egress autoscale policy review and qos config
- medium: provisioner debounce + leader-change throttle
- medium: add leader_renew_failures metric & alert
- long: root cause of peering jitter (kernel update / NIC config / upstream peering provider)

lena: agreed. I'll own the provisioner debounce PR. henry, can you coordinate the staged rollout?

henry: yep. I'll create a canary plan doc and link it in the ticket.

mira: thanks team. Keep this thread updated with the postmortem link and rollback if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
